title: Cinematic Blur & Depth-of-Field Focus Animations Architecture

blocks.content: Engineering notebook from `docs/CINEMATIC_BLUR_AND_FOCUS_ANIMATIONS.md`. This archive preserves the project’s original rationale, equations, performance reports and illustrative code. Historical paths, API names, claims and sketches can differ from the current engine. For copy-ready programs use the guides and demos; for current callable signatures use the source-derived API. Performance figures here describe reported experiments, not guaranteed frame rates.

blocks.text: Original document: [docs/CINEMATIC_BLUR_AND_FOCUS_ANIMATIONS.md](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/docs/CINEMATIC_BLUR_AND_FOCUS_ANIMATIONS.md). See [current limitations](/limitations) for concrete compatibility notes.
Cinematic visual storytelling frequently relies on **rack focus** (pulling focus between foreground and background), defocus transitions, and atmospheric blur pulses to direct audience attention.
Retiam provides a dedicated blur animation suite:

items: **[`BlurTarget`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/BlurTarget.ts)**: Polymorphic target resolver that unifies blur manipulation across [`RenderTarget`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/RenderTarget.ts), [`BlurPass`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/passes/BlurPass.ts), [`Sprite`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/entities/primitives/2d/Sprite.ts), and [`Entity`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Entity.ts) instances.

children: **[`BlurPulse`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/BlurPulse.ts)**: Temporary defocus pulse for emphasis or dreamlike state transitions.
**[`BlurTo`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/animation/BlurTo.ts)**: Smooth interpolation between arbitrary blur radii.

blocks.text: Different engine subsystems manage blur through different properties. `resolveBlurTarget()` standardizes this access into a uniform `ResolvedBlurTarget` interface:

items: **Immediate Initial Defocus**: The target's blur radius is clamped to `startRadius` on construction, preventing a single sharp frame from rendering prior to the start of the animation.
